issues.t: Automatic transmission slips, shifts hard or fails
issues.sym: Late or harsh shifts, the engine revving up between gears, slipping when warm, or the van losing reverse, second or overdrive. In the worst cases it will not move at all.
issues.why: The 4L60-E four-speed automatic behind the 4.3L works hard moving a heavy van, and heat breaks down the fluid and wears clutches and internal parts such as the sun gear shell. Transmission failure is the most costly problem owners report for these vans.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell with the engine warm. Dark or burnt fluid is a bad sign. If it slips or will not engage, stop towing or loading the van and get a transmission diagnosis; a rebuild or a replacement unit is usually needed. An add-on transmission cooler helps a rebuilt unit last.

issues.t: Slipping when hot and code P1870 from a worn valve body
issues.sym: The transmission feels like it slips or flares once it is fully warm, often after a long drive, and shifts can turn firm. The check engine light may come on with code P1870 (torque converter clutch slip).
issues.why: Wear inside the aluminum valve body, the part that routes fluid to the clutches, lets pressure leak away. Owners and shops tie this to code P1870 on the 4L60-E, and GM later revised the design.
issues.next: Have the code read and the fluid checked. Catching it early can mean replacing the valve body and related valves instead of rebuilding the whole transmission.

issues.t: ABS kicks in at low speed and the van rolls farther
issues.sym: When slowing to a stop, usually under about 5 mph on dry pavement, the pedal pulses and buzzes as if on ice and the van keeps rolling. Stopping distances get longer and the ABS light may come on.
issues.why: Rust builds up on the front wheel speed sensors and the toothed rings they read. The weak or uneven signal makes the ABS computer think a wheel is locking, so it lets off brake pressure when it should not. Owners report it widely on these vans.
issues.next: Leave extra room when stopping and get it checked soon. A shop can clean the sensor mounting areas and replace corroded sensors; if that does not cure it, the ABS module may be at fault. Do not simply pull the ABS fuse as a permanent fix.

issues.t: ABS warning light from a failed ABS control module
issues.sym: The ABS light stays on. Anti-lock braking is switched off, and some owners notice odd pulsing or a hard pedal before the light comes on.
issues.why: The electronic brake control module that runs the anti-lock system fails with age, often well past 100,000 miles. RepairPal has dozens of reports on these vans.
issues.next: Normal brakes still work, but drive gently and have the ABS codes read. Rule out a cheaper wheel speed sensor problem first, then replace or rebuild the module.

issues.t: Rusted brake and fuel lines leak
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly sinks toward the floor, brake fluid drips near a wheel, or you smell raw fuel around the van. A brake warning light may come on.
issues.why: The steel brake and fuel lines run along the underside and rust through with age, especially where roads are salted. Lines can also wear through where they rub on other parts.
issues.next: If the pedal goes soft or you smell fuel, stop driving and have it towed. Ask the shop to check every brake and fuel line, not just the one leaking, because the rest are usually in similar shape.

issues.t: Battery cable or wiring rubbed through by steering parts
issues.sym: A dead battery or no-start, sparks or a burning smell, everything electrical cutting out while driving, or the brake pedal sinking after a sharp turn. In some cases a fire started.
issues.why: The positive battery cable and a wiring harness near the front passenger wheel can rub against the steering linkage and suspension as the wheels turn. Once the insulation wears through, the wire shorts to the frame, which can melt nearby brake lines or damage the engine and ABS computers.
issues.next: Look along the battery cable and nearby wiring for shiny worn spots, melted insulation or rub marks. Have damaged wires replaced and secured with proper clips away from moving parts before they short.

issues.t: Brake lights and hazards can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The brake lights and rear hazard lights do not come on, and the hazard switch button may be stuck.
issues.why: The hazard switch inside the multifunction switch on the steering column can wear its contacts and open the circuit for both the brake lights and the hazards. NHTSA looked into it and GM recalled 2001 and early 2002 Safari and Astro vans (recall 05V-099).
issues.next: Have a helper check your brake lights. Ask a dealer whether recall 05V-099 was done; the fix is a new hazard switch with special grease, or a new multifunction switch.

issues.t: Brake lights fail from a worn turn signal switch
issues.sym: Brake lights, turn signals or hazards stop working, sometimes on and off.
issues.why: The brake light circuit runs through the turn signal (multifunction) switch on the steering column. Its contacts wear, and these earlier vans were not part of the later recall on the same part.
issues.next: Check the brake lights and signals. A shop can test the switch and replace it if the circuit is open there.

issues.t: Intake manifold gaskets leak coolant
issues.sym: Coolant puddles on top of the engine where the intake meets the cylinder heads, a sweet smell, a falling coolant level, or overheating. Coolant mixing into the oil can turn it milky.
issues.why: The 4.3L V6 uses intake gaskets that break down over time, which owners often link to the original Dex-Cool coolant. Coolant then seeps out of the joint, usually on the driver side.
issues.next: Top up the coolant and watch the level and temperature gauge. Get it fixed soon, because coolant in the oil or overheating can ruin the engine. The fix is new upper and lower intake gaskets and fresh coolant.

issues.t: Rough running from the central 'spider' fuel injector
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, misfires and a check engine light that keep coming back, even after new plugs and wires. Fuel economy drops.
issues.why: The 4.3L uses one central injector unit with lines and small poppet nozzles feeding each cylinder. The nozzles stick or clog and the unit can leak, so cylinders get the wrong amount of fuel.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read and a fuel pressure and injector test done. Replacing the central injector assembly usually cures it; a leaking unit is also a fire risk, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Misfires from worn ignition parts or vacuum leaks
issues.sym: Jerking at highway speed, a shaky idle, and a check engine light with code P0300 or a single-cylinder misfire code.
issues.why: The 4.3L fires its plugs through a distributor cap, rotor and long plug wires that wear out, and aging vacuum hoses split and let in extra air. Owners often find more than one of these at once.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replace the cap, rotor, wires and plugs as a set if they are old, and check the vacuum hoses for cracks. Do not keep driving with a flashing check engine light, since it can overheat the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Won't start after damp, cold weather from a wet distributor cap
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start after the van sits in cold, wet or icy weather. A new battery does not help.
issues.why: Moisture can collect inside the distributor cap, so the spark leaks away before it reaches the plugs.
issues.next: Have the cap and rotor checked. Replacing them, and making sure the cap seals well, usually ends the problem.

issues.t: Fuel pump fails and the engine stalls or won't start
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start, or it cuts out while driving and may restart later. You may not hear the pump hum when you turn the key.
issues.why: The electric pump inside the fuel tank wears out, and some owners have replaced it more than once.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested to confirm the pump is the cause. Replace the fuel filter at the same time. The tank has to come down, so this is not a quick job.

issues.t: Power steering failure also cuts brake assist
issues.sym: Steering suddenly turns heavy and the brake pedal becomes very hard at the same moment, sometimes after a whine or squeal from the engine.
issues.why: These vans use the power steering pump to power the brake booster. If the pump fails, leaks, or its belt or idler pulley lets go, you lose both power steering and power brakes together.
issues.next: Pull over carefully. Press the brake harder than usual; the brakes still work, just without help. Have the pump, hoses, belt and pulleys checked before driving again.

issues.t: Engine stalls while driving
issues.sym: The engine dies while driving or pulling away, sometimes with the battery light on, and may not restart for a while. Steering and braking get much harder.
issues.why: Owners trace it to several causes, including a failed crankshaft position sensor, a weak fuel pump and bad electrical connections. The cause has to be found with testing.
issues.next: Get the van off the road safely and have it checked while the problem is happening if you can. Stored codes and a fuel pressure test help pin it down.

issues.t: Gas pedal sticks or the van keeps accelerating
issues.sym: The pedal feels jerky or sticks, the engine stays at high revs after you lift off, or cruise control does not let go when you brake.
issues.why: A worn or fraying accelerator cable can bind or break, and dirty throttle parts can stick. Some owners also report cruise control that would not shut off.
issues.next: If it happens, shift to neutral, brake firmly and turn off the engine once stopped. Have the throttle cable, throttle body and cruise control parts inspected and replaced as needed.

issues.t: Low oil pressure and failed main bearings
issues.sym: The oil pressure gauge drops or the oil light comes on, followed by knocking from the bottom of the engine.
issues.why: A few owners of early vans report main bearing failure in the 4.3L that ended in an engine replacement.
issues.next: If oil pressure drops, stop the engine right away and check the oil level. Have the pressure tested with a gauge, because the dash sender can also fail.

issues.t: Power door locks stop working
issues.sym: One or more doors will not lock or unlock with the switch or remote, or a lock clicks without moving.
issues.why: The electric lock actuator inside the door wears out. It is one of the most reported problems on RepairPal for these vans.
issues.next: Test each door to find which actuator has failed. Replacing the actuator inside the door panel usually fixes it.

issues.t: Outside door handles break
issues.sym: A door handle feels loose or snaps, and the door will not open from outside.
issues.why: The plastic outside handles crack with age and use. RepairPal has more than 100 owner reports, on every door.
issues.next: Replace the handle before it fails completely. On the sliding door, a broken handle can leave passengers unable to get out from the outside.

issues.t: Power windows stop going up
issues.sym: A window goes down but will not come back up, moves slowly, or makes grinding noises.
issues.why: The window motor or regulator inside the door wears out, and some owners have replaced them more than once.
issues.next: Have the motor and regulator checked. Many shops replace them together because they wear at the same time.

issues.t: Dashboard gauges stop working or read wrong
issues.sym: The speedometer, fuel gauge or other gauges freeze, drop to zero or show wrong readings, sometimes along with the odometer.
issues.why: The instrument cluster develops faults with age, often in the small gauge motors or the circuit board.
issues.next: Do not rely on the fuel gauge until it is fixed. A shop that rebuilds instrument clusters can usually repair the original.

issues.t: Brake shudder from warped front rotors
issues.sym: A shaking steering wheel or pulsing pedal when braking, a thumping noise from the front, or the van pulling to one side.
issues.why: Front brake rotors on this heavy van warp from heat, and some owners report replacing them repeatedly.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Replace them with quality parts and tighten the wheels to the correct torque, which helps prevent warping.

issues.t: Steering knuckle can separate from worn lower ball joint (recall)
issues.sym: A popping or clunking noise from the front when turning or backing up.
issues.why: The rubber boot on the lower ball joint can rub on the steering knuckle and tear. Dirt and water then wear out the joint, and in the worst case the knuckle can separate, letting the wheel fold under and cutting the brake hose. GM recall 03044 (NHTSA 03V-328).
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the recall was done; the fix is new steering knuckles on both sides. If you still hear popping afterwards, have the ball joints inspected.

issues.t: Windshield wipers work on and off or quit (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop or work only sometimes, which is dangerous in rain or snow.
issues.why: Solder joints on the circuit board inside the wiper motor crack. GM recalled these vans (recall 03V-159).
issues.next: Check with a dealer that the recall was done. The fix is a new wiper motor circuit board and cover at no charge.

issues.t: Rear bucket seat belt can tear in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning; the right rear bucket seat belt may not hold in a crash.
issues.why: The webbing for the outer belt on the right rear bucket seat could separate in a crash (recall 97V-057).
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the recall was done on your van.

issues.t: Built-in child seat belt can lock up (recall)
issues.sym: The harness on the built-in child seat stays locked and will not pull out.
issues.why: Some integrated child seats were missing small springs in the belt retractor, so the belt can lock in the stowed position and be unusable (recall 99V-009).
issues.next: If your van has the built-in child seat, ask a dealer whether the recall was done and do not use a seat that will not adjust.

issues.t: Engine overheats
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, steam or a coolant smell comes from under the van, or the low coolant light comes on.
issues.why: Overheating is the top reported problem for the 2002 Safari. On this engine it usually follows coolant loss from leaking intake gaskets, a failing water pump or a blocked radiator.
issues.next: Stop and let the engine cool if the gauge goes high. Have the cooling system pressure-tested to find the leak before the head gaskets are damaged.
